traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Symplocaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins pinnate; leaves evergreen or deciduous; stipules absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, rarely polygamous; ovary usually inferior, rarely half inferior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers solitary, in panicles, in racemes or in spikes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit usually drupe, sometimes berry; parts of each whorl 5; stamens (4-) 5 to 35; carpels 2 to 5. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
